questions.q: What is sustainable development, and what strategies can help achieve it?

answer.text: Sustainable development is development that meets the needs of the present generation without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. It requires that we use natural resources carefully, keep pollution within limits, and preserve the environment so that it can continue to support life. In short, it balances economic growth with social equity and environmental protection.

Several strategies can promote it. The use of non-conventional and renewable sources of energy, such as solar and wind power, reduces dependence on polluting fossil fuels. Cleaner fuels like LPG and CNG in cities and biogas in villages cut pollution. Recycling of materials, water harvesting, and afforestation conserve resources and restore the environment. Reviving traditional knowledge and practices also helps.

answer: By adopting such measures, growth can continue without destroying the environment on which future generations depend.

questions.q: Why has economic development often come at the cost of the environment?

answer.text: has frequently damaged the environment because growth uses natural resources heavily and generates waste.

list: Industry, farming and cities draw down resources like water, minerals, forests and fossil fuels faster than they renew
Production and consumption release pollution into the air, water and land
Depletion of resources, pollution, deforestation and global warming threaten health and future growth
Treating the environment as free and limitless has led to a supply-demand imbalance, making sustainable development necessary

questions.q: What are the key strategies for achieving sustainable development?

answer.text: means meeting present needs without harming the ability of future generations to meet theirs, and several strategies help achieve it.

list: Using non-conventional, renewable energy — solar, wind, biogas — instead of polluting fossil fuels
Adopting cleaner technology and efficient use of resources to cut waste and pollution
Protecting forests, water and biodiversity, and recycling materials
Spreading environmental awareness and enforcing pollution laws so that growth and the environment go together
